what: Bio-Rad makes laboratory instruments and reagents: droplet digital PCR systems for counting DNA molecules, protein analysis equipment, and quality control materials for clinical laboratories.
customers: Research laboratories, biotech companies and clinical diagnostic laboratories.
money: droplet digital PCR, protein analysis and chromatography
quality controls, blood typing and infectious disease testing
moat: Droplet digital PCR is a technology it largely owns, and clinical quality control materials are written into laboratory accreditation procedures.
risks: Revenue has fallen every year since 2021, from $2.9B to $2.6B
Reported earnings are dominated by the value of its stake in Sartorius, not by operations
Only three analysts cover it and their target is below the price
opportunities: 9.7 times earnings with $1.5B of cash against $1.4B of debt
A large shareholding in Sartorius worth a substantial part of the market value
Droplet digital PCR is being adopted for cancer monitoring, a growing clinical use
watch: Core organic revenue growth separate from the Sartorius stake's value.
